title: Zariski local criterion for a trace-defined derived adjunction
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work on unbounded derived categories of modules with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Supply $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ and a trace $\tau:Rf_*K\to\mathcal O_S$. Set $G(M)=Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$, using [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Give $G$ its trace-defined natural transformation $\epsilon_M:Rf_*G(M)\simeq M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{1\otimes\tau}M$ via the projection formula. Suppose for every affine open $V\subset S$ the analogous functor $G_V$ on $X_V=f^{-1}V$ is right adjoint to $Rf_{V,*}$ with exactly the restricted trace-defined counit. Then composition with $\epsilon$ gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,G(M))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(Rf_*E,M)$$
for all $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ and $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(S)$. No qcqs hypothesis on the individual schemes $S,X$, finite cover, or boundedness of $E,M$ is required.

source.place: Agent local-to-global consequence of the trace-adjunction construction, section-trace, equations equation-sheafy-trace and equation-global-hom; internal-Hom restriction: cohomology.tex Tag 08DL; projection formula: perfect.tex Tag 08EU (lemma-cohomology-base-change).

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is separated, so it is quasi-separated: a separated morphism, whose diagonal is a closed immersion, has quasi-compact diagonal [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The quasi-coherent pullback/tensor theorem makes $G(M)$ quasi-coherent, and the direct-image theorem makes $Rf_*E$ and $Rf_*K$ quasi-coherent. Apply the unbounded projection formula to $K,M$, with symmetry of the tensor factors, to form the stated counit $\epsilon_M$. These results assume only that the morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, not that its source or target is quasi-compact.

Fix $E,M$ and write $N=G(M)$, $A=Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(E,N)$ and $B=R\mathcal Hom_S(Rf_*E,M)$ in the full module derived category of $S$. Form $a:A\to B$ as the evaluation-mate direct-image comparison followed by $R\mathcal Hom_S(Rf_*E,\epsilon_M)$. For an open $V$ put $U=f^{-1}V$, $g=f|_U$. The comparison-on-open-Ext lemma, the open Ext/hypercohomology identification and its naturality in the second variable together with the open-restriction isomorphisms $(Rf_*E)|_V\cong Rg_*(E|_U)$ and $(Rf_*N)|_V\cong Rg_*(N|_U)$ of the restriction-of-direct-image lemma, identify $H^q(V,a)$ with
$$u\longmapsto (\epsilon_M|_V)[q]\circ Rg_*u,$$
from $\operatorname{Hom}_U(E|_U,N|_U[q])$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_V((Rf_*E)|_V,M|_V[q])$. This also identifies the formula for $V=S$, without affineness. All these identifications commute with smaller-open restriction.

For affine $V$, restriction of derived pullback and tensor identifies $N|_U$ with $G_V(M|_V)$; restriction of direct image identifies $(Rf_*E)|_V$ with $Rg_*(E|_U)$. The hypothesis says precisely that the restricted $\epsilon$ is the local adjunction counit. Hence the formula of step 2 is bijective for every $q$: use the local adjunction on $E|_U[-q]$ and $M|_V$, then shift the Hom groups. Exact restriction preserves quasi-coherent cohomology, so these are objects of the categories in the hypothesis. No assertion that an arbitrary Hom presheaf is a sheaf has been used.

Apply the unbounded direct-image/section-presheaf theorem to the identity of $S$: the sheafification of $V\mapsto H^q(V,A)$ is $\mathcal H^q(A)$, naturally, and likewise for $B$. Step 3 gives bijections on every affine open. These opens are a neighbourhood basis at every point, so on each stalk the induced map is a bijection: a germ has an affine representative, and both equality of germs and its preimage can be tested after shrinking to an affine neighbourhood. Thus every $\mathcal H^q(a)$ is an isomorphism. By the defining quasi-isomorphism criterion for the derived category, $a$ is an isomorphism. Apply the functor $H^0(S,-)$ to it. The section-presheaf theorem and the open Ext comparison identify its source with $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,N)$ and its target with $\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_*E,M)$. Step 2 identifies this bijection as $u\mapsto\epsilon_M\circ Rf_*u$. Functoriality of the comparisons and naturality of $\epsilon$ give naturality in $E,M$. The stalk argument uses all affine neighbourhoods and requires no finite cover.
